transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I’m here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just about paperwork and missed payments. But I know that's not true. The bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. They keep handing me documents, but no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing going on for almost two years now.
Have they done anything to you that you believe is impossible by ordinary means, like controlling your thoughts or sending you messages in a supernatural way?

No, nothing like that. I mean, nobody is controlling my mind or using magic or anything supernatural. It's not... it's nothing like that. 

It's just regular people doing things behind my back. They use the system—like emails, scheduling at work, manipulating the mortgage paperwork. It's not impossible by any means, it's just a highly coordinated effort to get me out of my home.
During this time, have you had a period when you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?

No, not at all. I mean... I get tired just like anyone else. I definitely haven't felt unusually energized. 

If anything, dealing with all of this—the bank, the people at work—it's exhausting. I still need my normal amount of sleep. I haven't experienced anything like what you're describing, I just feel worn out from having to constantly watch my back.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

No, I don't hear voices. It's nothing like that. I just hear regular conversations, you know, people talking in the breakroom or whispering when they think I'm not listening. But no, I don't hear voices when I'm alone.
When you explain what has been happening, do other people ever tell you that your speech is hard to follow or doesn’t make sense?

No, people don't say that. I speak perfectly clearly. I mean, they might not want to hear what I'm saying because it's inconvenient for them, or they're in on it, but my speech makes total sense. I just lay out the facts—the emails, the discrepancies with the bank—and they just act like they don't understand because they're trying to gaslight me. But no, there's nothing wrong with the way I talk.
Have you had any major medical or neurological illness, such as seizures or a head injury?
No, nothing like that. I haven't had any head injuries or seizures, and I don't have any major medical conditions. I'm perfectly healthy in that regard.
Have you found yourself losing interest in seeing people or doing your usual activities?

No, not really. I mean, I still do all my usual stuff. I go to work, I manage my team at the store... I haven't lost interest in my life. I might be a little more careful about who I spend time with outside of work, just because I have to watch who I trust right now, but no, I still enjoy my regular activities.
During this time, have you had a period when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

No, I haven't been depressed. I mean, obviously it's incredibly frustrating dealing with all of this, with people lying to my face and everything, but I'm not sitting around feeling sad or down all day. I just want to get to the bottom of what's going on. So no, I wouldn't say I've felt depressed.
Aside from this situation with the bank and people at work, have you had any other strongly held beliefs that others say are not true?

No, I haven't. I mean... no. It's really just this specific issue. I don't go around believing strange things, if that's what you're asking. Everything else in my life is completely normal. I just know what I'm seeing with the bank and my team, even if other people are denying it or calling me crazy. But besides that, no, there's nothing else.
Has anything happened in this situation that other people would say is clearly impossible in real life?

No, nothing like that. I mean, it's not like aliens are involved or someone's reading my mind. It's just a coordinated effort to mess with my accounts and my job. People lying, covering things up, maybe hacking into the bank's system... that's all stuff that happens in the real world. It's not impossible, it's just happening to me right now.
How long have you been convinced that the bank and people at work are working together to push you out of your house?

It's been going on for about a year and nine months now. That's when the foreclosure notices started showing up, and the bank started calling all the time, just completely taking over our home life. So yeah, almost two years of this.
Have you ever felt that other people could read your thoughts?

No. Like I said a minute ago, no one is reading my mind. It's nothing like that. My thoughts are my own. Everything they are doing is... well, it's happening out in the real world, behind my back. But no, they definitely can't hear what I'm thinking.
Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

No. I don't see things that aren't there. Everything I see is... well, it's real. It's the actual paperwork from the bank, or the people at the store watching me. I'm not seeing visions or anything made up, if that's what you're getting at. I just see exactly what is happening.
Have you ever felt that other people were putting thoughts into your mind?

No, not at all. Just like with the mind-reading thing... my thoughts are completely my own. Nobody is planting ideas or putting thoughts into my head. 

Everything they're doing to me is happening on the outside—the bank notices, the whispering at work, all of that. But they don't have access to my brain. My mind is just my own.
Because of this situation, have you had trouble keeping up with your work or daily responsibilities?

Well, mostly, no. I mean, I still get up for work every day. I supervise my team, handle the schedules, deal with customer issues... I take care of myself just fine, as long as the foreclosure isn't involved. 

The problems really only start when... well, when I get certain mail, or if the bank calls, or if I see paperwork at work that seems tied to what is happening with my house. That's when it gets difficult. But if none of that is going on, I do my job and handle my responsibilities normally.
Do you believe your house is being targeted because of a special identity or role you have that other people do not know about?

No, no, it's nothing like that. I'm not a secret agent or someone famous, if that's what you mean. I'm just a regular person trying to keep my home. I don't have any special identity or hidden role. The bank is just coming after my house, and they're using people at my work and in my neighborhood to do it. It has nothing to do with who I am, it's just about what they're trying to take from me.
Do people in your community or family generally share this belief that the bank and your coworkers are coordinating to force you out of your home?

No, they don't. Actually, they don't believe me at all. My sister thinks I'm just stressed about money, and my neighbors... well, they either don't know or they're part of it, I'm not sure which. But no one I've tried to talk to seems to understand what's actually happening. They just tell me I'm overreacting or that banks don't operate like that. But I know what I'm seeing.
Have you ever been told that you showed much less emotion in your facial expression or voice than usual?

No, I haven't. Nobody's ever said anything like that to me. I mean, I think I show emotion just like anyone else would, especially when I'm frustrated about all this bank stuff. But no, I haven't had anyone tell me my face or voice seems flat or anything like that.
Have you been using any drugs or medications that could affect your thinking?

No, I don't use drugs. I don't even drink, really. And the only medication I take is just over-the-counter stuff, like ibuprofen if I have a headache. Nothing that would mess with my head or make me imagine things, if that's what you're getting at. I'm completely clear-headed.

target_item.manifestation: When the foreclosure is not involved, I still get up for work, supervise my team, handle schedules and customer issues, and take care of myself. The problems mostly start when mail, bank calls, or workplace paperwork seem tied to what I believe is happening with the house.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about my ability to keep up with work and daily responsibilities, which directly relates to my level of functioning (whether it is impaired or not).

patient.answer:
Well, mostly, no. I mean, I still get up for work every day. I supervise my team, handle the schedules, deal with customer issues... I take care of myself just fine, as long as the foreclosure isn't involved. 

The problems really only start when... well, when I get certain mail, or if the bank calls, or if I see paperwork at work that seems tied to what is happening with my house. That's when it gets difficult. But if none of that is going on, I do my job and handle my responsibilities normally.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the belief is non-bizarre and circumscribed enough to support delusional disorder rather than schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis with broader bizarre delusions.
doctor.question: Do you believe your house is being targeted because of a special identity or role you have that other people do not know about?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient believes they are being targeted because of a special identity or role (grandiose delusion), which is not covered in the symptom profile. The profile describes a persecutory delusion about a bank and employer colluding to push them out of their house, but does not mention any special identity or role.

patient.answer: No, no, it's nothing like that. I'm not a secret agent or someone famous, if that's what you mean. I'm just a regular person trying to keep my home. I don't have any special identity or hidden role. The bank is just coming after my house, and they're using people at my work and in my neighborhood to do it. It has nothing to do with who I am, it's just about what they're trying to take from me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief is culturally shared or idiosyncratic, to distinguish a primary delusional disorder from a non-pathological belief and help separate F22 from schizophrenia-spectrum alternatives.
doctor.question: Do people in your community or family generally share this belief that the bank and your coworkers are coordinating to force you out of your home?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient's beliefs are shared by their community or family (cultural/subcultural context of the delusion), which is not explicitly covered in the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer: No, they don't. Actually, they don't believe me at all. My sister thinks I'm just stressed about money, and my neighbors... well, they either don't know or they're part of it, I'm not sure which. But no one I've tried to talk to seems to understand what's actually happening. They just tell me I'm overreacting or that banks don't operate like that. But I know what I'm seeing.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there have ever been prominent negative symptoms, which would support schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever been told that you showed much less emotion in your facial expression or voice than usual?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about flat affect or blunted affect (negative symptoms of schizophrenia), which is not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: No, I haven't. Nobody's ever said anything like that to me. I mean, I think I show emotion just like anyone else would, especially when I'm frustrated about all this bank stuff. But no, I haven't had anyone tell me my face or voice seems flat or anything like that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief is plausibly explained by substance or medication use, helping distinguish a primary delusional disorder from an organic/substance-induced psychosis.
doctor.question: Have you been using any drugs or medications that could affect your thinking?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about substance use (drugs or medications) that could affect my thinking, which is not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: No, I don't use drugs. I don't even drink, really. And the only medication I take is just over-the-counter stuff, like ibuprofen if I have a headache. Nothing that would mess with my head or make me imagine things, if that's what you're getting at. I'm completely clear-headed.

inference.note: Persistent non-bizarre persecutory delusion for ~21 months with otherwise preserved functioning; no hallucinations, thought disorder, negative symptoms, mood episodes, substance use, or medical/neurological cause. This rules against F20.9, F23, F25.9, and F06.2.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a single, persistent non-bizarre persecutory delusional belief lasting about 1 year 9 months that the bank, coworkers, and others are coordinating to force foreclosure. The belief is not culturally shared, is not accompanied by hallucinations, thought insertion/broadcasting, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, manic or depressive episodes, substance use, or medical/neurological causes. Functioning is largely preserved outside the delusion, supporting persistent delusional disorder.
